title: Damage Control
text: Your secret is getting heavy: “{secret}.” People are starting to ask questions.

ok.text: {about} is quiet for a while, then says “thanks for telling me”. It still hurts, but it's over.

fail.text: {about} takes it badly. Very badly. At least it's out.

ok.text: It costs you. The secret goes back in the ground. For now.

effects.remember: Paid to keep a secret buried: {secret}.

fail.text: It costs you. The secret goes back in the ground, for now. You tell the person you paid what it was for, in detail.

blabber.text: You pay them, then explain the whole secret so they know what they're keeping quiet about. They're now very well informed.

ok.text: It works. {friend} gets the blame. You get to keep a friend, technically.

fail.text: {friend} has an alibi: {friend.he} was in a fountain, on camera. Now everyone's looking at you.

effects.remember: Tried to blame {friend}. It made everything worse.

title: The Awkward Dinner
text: At dinner someone says “funny story…” and you just know it's about this: “{secret}.” You have about four seconds.

choices.label: Tell the story yourself first, as a joke

ok.text: Everyone laughs. It's just a funny story now. Nobody can use it against you. Genius.

effects.remember: Turned your secret into a dinner party joke: {secret}.

fail.text: Nobody laughs. Somebody gasps. You keep going, which makes it worse.

effects.remember: Told your secret as a joke at dinner. Nobody laughed.

ok.text: Gravy everywhere. Chaos. By the time it's cleaned up, the story is forgotten. For now.

effects.remember: Saved yourself with a gravy spill.

fail.text: You knock over the gravy. Everyone waits politely while you clean it up. Then: “Anyway, funny story…”

choices.label: Kick {crush} under the table for help

ok.text: {crush} starts a long story about {crush.his} cousin's divorce. Nobody ever gets back to yours.

cast.did: changed the subject like a pro

fail.text: {crush} says “ow, why are you kicking me?” Everyone looks at you.
